top_stories.title: Indian founder Swapnil Srivastav gets rejected for US visa for 'not enough ties to home country' - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Indian** entrepreneur Swapnil Srivastav, co-founder of a bamboo-based kids' wear brand, was recently denied a US tourist visa despite having a successful business and strong ties to India. **Srivastav** argued that his company employs over 100 people, receives funding from top investors, and serves millions of Indian families. He plans to reapply for the visa but faces a trend of other **Indian** entrepreneurs facing similar rejections due to concerns about their ties to India.

top_stories.title: Alicia Hempleman-Adams becomes first British woman to cross Atlantic in hydrogen balloon | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Alicia Hempleman-Adams**, a 36-year-old British explorer, successfully completed the first transatlantic journey in a hydrogen gas balloon from Maine to Europe.  She flew alongside fellow balloonists **Bert Padelt** and **Peter Cuneo**, facing harsh conditions including freezing temperatures and strong winds during the four-day flight. The team encountered challenges throughout the journey, requiring constant monitoring of weather conditions and adaptation to changing circumstances.  **Hempleman-Adams**, who holds several aviation records, is now the first British woman to cross the Atlantic in a hydrogen gas balloon, following in her father's footsteps.

top_stories.title: Indian students asked 'how do I get a data engineering job in the US': Tech founder says $100K H-1B visa fee made the answer depressing - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Zach Wilson**, a former **Meta** engineer, expressed pride in being an American after a federal court struck down the $100,000 fee imposed by the **Trump administration** on H-1B visa holders.  Wilson stated that he had to visit India this year due to the fees and believes the US is losing out on talent by not welcoming foreign workers. He also acknowledged the backlash from some social media users who criticized his stance on training American students, but defended his position by stating he has never faced discrimination under Indian managers.

top_stories.title: Promoter sells Rs 1,024 crore worth of Ajanta Pharma shares in block deal to Kotak MF and ABSL MF - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ajanta Pharma** saw significant share purchases by **Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund** and **Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund**, acquiring 21.02 lakh and 13.48 lakh shares respectively at a price of Rs 2,968 per share. The pharmaceutical company has been performing well in the market due to steady earnings growth, healthy margins, and a robust balance sheet.  **Elara Capital** raised its FY27E-FY28E core earnings estimates for **Ajanta Pharma**, citing strong US generics business growth and a positive fourth quarter performance.

top_stories.title: After Japan, Nepal Bans Import Of Indian Mangoes Over This Issue
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Nepal** has banned imports of Indian mangoes due to excessive pesticide levels detected in shipments. The ban, imposed by the **Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development**, began around April-May and is expected to disrupt exports during the crucial summer mango season. Local traders warn that domestic supply may not meet demand, potentially leading to shortages.  The government claims the move will promote local fruit production but faces concerns from exporters who fear it could damage India's agricultural quality control systems.

top_stories.title: Fake IDs, Fake Cop Badges, Fake Money: Bengal Killer Couple's 'World Of Fake'
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Delhi Police** recovered fake IDs, police badges, counterfeit currency bundles, and over 100 shirts from the accused couple's home in connection with the murder of **Delhi University Assistant Professor Debosmita Paul**. The investigation revealed that the couple had planned the attack meticulously, conducting reconnaissance for several days before the murder. They also attempted to conceal their identities after the crime by changing clothes multiple times and taking a circuitous route to avoid suspicion.  The police are now investigating if the accused were involved in any other crimes.

top_stories.title: PM Modi speaks to Amir of Kuwait, expresses concern over escalation of tensions in West Asia | India News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** spoke with **Sheikh Meshal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al Sabah**, the Amir of Kuwait, on Tuesday to discuss escalating tensions in West Asia.  The conversation came days after an Indian national was killed in an Iranian attack on Kuwait International Airport and followed India's condemnation of the attacks on Kuwait's sovereignty and territorial integrity. **Modi** reiterated his call for de-escalation, dialogue, and diplomacy to restore peace and stability while thanking the Amir for his concern for the safety of the large Indian community in Kuwait.

top_stories.title: Indian students asked 'how do I get a data engineering job in the US': Tech founder says $100K H-1B visa fee made the answer depressing - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Zach Wilson**, a former **Meta** engineer, expressed pride in being an American after a federal court struck down the $100,000 fee imposed by the **Trump administration** on H-1B visa holders.  Wilson stated that the fees discouraged Indian students from seeking data engineering jobs in the US, leading him to visit India for job opportunities. He acknowledged the global talent pool and highlighted the importance of immigration and new ideas for American innovation.

top_stories.title: Bengal BJP govt’s first month: From anti-corruption drive, border fencing to new welfare schemes | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: The newly formed **BJP** government in West Bengal has taken several significant steps in its first month, including transferring land to the Border Security Force for border fencing and expanding the state's flagship subsidized food program.  The government has also launched an anti-corruption drive, arresting over 300 TMC leaders accused of corruption. Chief Minister **Suvendu Adhikari** has promised to tackle issues like illegal infiltration and address concerns about welfare schemes. However, the government has faced criticism for its "bulldozer culture" approach to evicting street hawkers without proper rehabilitation.  The BJP government is still in its early stages and faces a long road ahead.

top_stories.title: Meat shops out of Varanasi? New civic body plan has traders and Opposition up in arms | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Varanasi Municipal Corporation** has proposed relocating meat, fish, and poultry shops to the city's outskirts, citing hygiene concerns and preservation of religious character. The proposal, approved by the executive committee and municipal corporation, aims to create designated markets with proper facilities. However, the move has sparked criticism from opposition parties and traders who argue that it will negatively impact livelihoods and inconvenience consumers.  The **Samajwadi Party** and **UP Congress** have questioned the selective action against meat shops while liquor outlets remain untouched. Traders have expressed concerns about accessibility, customer convenience, and economic losses associated with relocating their businesses. They propose alternative solutions like enclosed modern outlets or restrictions around temple areas instead of full relocation.
